name: MonarchTableOfContents
title: TableOfContents
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of entries made with androidx.compose.foundation.clickable and androidx.compose.material3.Text; rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy reads androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyListState.layoutInfo in derivedStateOf
summary: In-page navigation built from the page's headings: a list of entries that marks the section being read and asks the app to scroll to the one chosen, with a scroll spy for a LazyColumn.
whenToUse: On long reading screens with several headed sections, such as documentation, policies or reports, usually in a bottom sheet opened from the top app bar on a phone and beside the content on a large screen.
whenNotToUse: For moving between separate screens, use navigation (a bar, a rail or tabs). For a short page that fits on one or two screens, leave it out.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableOfContents(items: List<MonarchTableOfContentsItem>, selectedId: String?, onSelect: (id: String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, showTitle: Boolean = true, title: String? = null, currentLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchTableOfContentsItem(title: String, id: String, level: Int = 2)
@Composable fun rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy(state: LazyListState, sections: Map<String, Int>, topInset: Dp = MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp): State<String?>

options.name: items
options.description: The entries in page order, each with a title, the id of its section and a heading level (2 by default).

options.name: selectedId
options.description: The id of the section being read, or null before the first heading. rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy keeps it in step with scrolling.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Scrolls to the chosen section, usually LazyListState.animateScrollToItem, and closes the sheet.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the entries can be chosen. When not, they use the disabled text color.

options.name: showTitle
options.description: Whether the title is shown. When hidden it still names the list for TalkBack.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "On this page".

options.name: currentLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Current section", read as the state of the current entry.

options.name: sections (spy)
options.description: The id of each section and the index of its heading item in the LazyColumn.

options.name: topInset (spy)
options.description: The height of anything covering the top of the list. A heading counts as scrolled past once it goes under it.

states.name: current
states.description: The entry's text is in the default color and a semibold weight, with an accent line beside it, and reads "Current section".

states.name: other
states.description: Muted text with a subtle line beside it.

states.name: nested
states.description: An entry with a deeper level is indented one step for each level below the shallowest entry.

states.name: no current section
states.description: With selectedId null, no entry is marked, as before the first heading reaches the top.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false every entry uses the disabled text color and ignores taps.

appearance: Entries in the body style on whatever surface holds the list, each with a 2dp line at the start: the accent solid color beside the current entry and the subtle border color beside the others. The title is a label in the muted text color. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TableOfContents reads h2 and h3 elements from the DOM, spies with IntersectionObserver and writes #id to the URL. Compose has no DOM, so the app passes the entries, and rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy reads the LazyColumn's layout with the same rule (the first heading in the top 40%, else the last scrolled past). There is no URL hash. The web's activeId and onActiveChange are selectedId and onSelect. The parity map named a LazyColumn for the list; a contents list is short and is usually placed in a sheet or a scrolling column, where a lazy list cannot be nested, so it is a Column. The web moves focus to the heading after scrolling; on Android TalkBack focus stays on the list, and the app can move it with a FocusRequester on the heading. iOS builds the same component with a view modifier spy.
accessibility: The list is one traversal group; the visible title is a heading, and when it is hidden it names the list.
Each entry is a clickable element with its title as the name and a touch target at least 48dp high across the full width.
The current entry reads the state "Current section" and is marked by an accent line and a heavier weight as well as by color.
Entries wrap instead of being cut at large font sizes.
The indent is a start padding, so nesting follows the reading direction right to left.
Each entry draws the Monarch focus ring when it has keyboard focus.
edgeCases: An empty list shows only the title.
A selectedId that matches no entry marks none.
Entries with levels 2 and 4 and nothing at 3 indent the level 4 entries two steps.
The spy returns null until the first heading reaches the top 40% of the list.
When the last section is too short to reach the top, the spy keeps the section scrolled past before it; the app may mark the chosen section itself after onSelect.

examples.title: Scroll-spy over an article
examples.setupTemplate:
val state = rememberLazyListState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val articleSections = listOf(
    Triple({{sections.0.id}}, {{sections.0.title}}, {{sections.0.level}}) to listOf({{sections.0.body.0}}, {{sections.0.body.1}}),
    Triple({{sections.1.id}}, {{sections.1.title}}, {{sections.1.level}}) to listOf({{sections.1.body.0}}, {{sections.1.body.1}}),
    Triple({{sections.2.id}}, {{sections.2.title}}, {{sections.2.level}}) to listOf({{sections.2.body.0}}, {{sections.2.body.1}}),
    Triple({{sections.3.id}}, {{sections.3.title}}, {{sections.3.level}}) to listOf({{sections.3.body.0}}, {{sections.3.body.1}}),
    Triple({{sections.4.id}}, {{sections.4.title}}, {{sections.4.level}}) to listOf({{sections.4.body.0}}, {{sections.4.body.1}}),
    Triple({{sections.5.id}}, {{sections.5.title}}, {{sections.5.level}}) to listOf({{sections.5.body.0}}, {{sections.5.body.1}}),
)
val sections = articleSections.mapIndexed { index, (meta, _) -> meta.first to index * 3 }.toMap()
val current by rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy(state, sections)
examples.setup:
val state = rememberLazyListState()
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
val articleSections = listOf(
    Triple("toc-demo-overview", "Overview", 2) to listOf("A paragraph about overview. Scroll this area and the current section is highlighted in the list beside it.", "Another paragraph so each section takes up some room."),
    Triple("toc-demo-setup", "Setup", 2) to listOf("A paragraph about setup. Scroll this area and the current section is highlighted in the list beside it.", "Another paragraph so each section takes up some room."),
    Triple("toc-demo-accounts", "Accounts", 3) to listOf("Details about accounts.", "More details, to make the section tall enough to scroll past."),
    Triple("toc-demo-permissions", "Permissions", 3) to listOf("Details about permissions.", "More details, to make the section tall enough to scroll past."),
    Triple("toc-demo-usage", "Daily use", 2) to listOf("A paragraph about daily use. Scroll this area and the current section is highlighted in the list beside it.", "Another paragraph so each section takes up some room."),
    Triple("toc-demo-questions", "Questions", 2) to listOf("A paragraph about questions. Scroll this area and the current section is highlighted in the list beside it.", "Another paragraph so each section takes up some room."),
)
val sections = articleSections.mapIndexed { index, (meta, _) -> meta.first to index * 3 }.toMap()
val current by rememberMonarchTableOfContentsSpy(state, sections)

examples.title: Nested entries, title hidden
examples.code:
MonarchTableOfContents(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchTableOfContentsItem(title = "Install", id = "install"),
        MonarchTableOfContentsItem(title = "With Gradle", id = "gradle", level = 3),
        MonarchTableOfContentsItem(title = "With Maven", id = "maven", level = 3),
    ),
    selectedId = selected,
    onSelect = { selected = it },
    showTitle = false,
)
